# tails — full notes for coding agents

Import: `import tails`. PyPI / pip name: `rare-tails` (the name `tails` is
taken on PyPI). Repo: https://github.com/rare-labs/tails
Docs: https://rare-labs.github.io/tails/

## Purpose

Extreme-value analysis in Python, designed to run one series or a large batch
in a single call (JAX `vmap` + a Newton optimiser with exact Hessians).

Use it for return levels, return periods, non-stationary GEV/GPD/POT, and
intensity–duration–frequency curves. If the user has one pandas time series
and wants diagnostic plots first, mention pyextremes. If they already use
xclim, mention that xclim frequency analysis returns a point return level on
a DataArray; tails adds profile-likelihood intervals, covariate models, and
IDF.

## Install

pip install rare-tails
# extras: xarray, plots, bayes, dev, docs, all
# Python >= 3.10. CPU by default (jax[cpu]); GPU needs a CUDA build of jax.

## API

tails.fit_gev(data, loc=None, scale=None, shape=None, mask=None, method="mle")
  data: shape (*batch, n). NaN = missing. method: "mle" | "gmle" | "lmom".
  Returns GEVFit.
  fit.params is a dict with natural parameters loc, scale, shape (arrays).
  fit.return_level(periods, ci="profile"|"delta"|"bootstrap", alpha=0.05)
  fit.coef, fit.se, fit.summary(), fit.converged, fit.nobs, fit.loglik.

tails.fit_gpd(data, threshold=None, ...)
tails.fit_pot(data, threshold, npy=365.25, ...)
  POT return_level supports ci=None or "delta" only.

tails.block_maxima, decluster_runs, extremal_index
tails.mean_residual_life, parameter_stability, select_threshold

from tails.idf import IDFData, fit_idf, scaling_test
  data = IDFData.from_eccc("701S001")
  fit_idf(data, "general"|"simple", "matern"|"exponential"|None)
  scaling_test(data, "simple"|"general") -> p-value
  idf.quantile_ci(durations, periods, method="hessian"|"sandwich"|"bootstrap")
  idf.plot(periods=(2,10,25,100), ci="hessian")  # log-log curves, CI ribbons,
                                                 # empirical T-year points in mm/h vs hours
  fit.plot_diagnostics(ci="profile")             # QQ/PP with bands, RL ribbon, density
  rl.plot()                                      # ReturnLevels ribbon

from tails.datasets import load_eccc_quebec, load_idfcurves, parse_eccc_idf, eccc_daily, eccc_hourly
  eccc_daily("701S001", 2020) / eccc_hourly(station, (2019, 2020))
  Official API: https://api.weather.gc.ca (cached under $TAILS_CACHE or ~/.cache/tails).
  load_eccc_quebec() -> DataFrame with station_id, name, lat, lon, elevation,
  year, and duration columns 5min, 10min, 15min, 30min, 1h, 2h, 6h, 12h, 24h.
  151 Québec stations, ECCC IDF v3.40.

import tails.xarray as tx
  tx.fit_gev(da, dim="time"); tx.return_level(ds, [20, 100])

from tails.bayes import fit_gev_bayes   # requires rare-tails[bayes]

## Worked example (real bundled data — do not invent other numbers)

Station 701S001, QUEBEC JEAN LESAGE INTL, 64 years (1961–2024), 24-hour
annual maxima. Wettest year: 2005, 105.4 mm.

fit = tails.fit_gev(y)  # y = the 24h column
# GEVFit(loc=51.66±1.6, log_scale=2.453±0.097, shape=-0.02595±0.078, loglik=-256.9124)
# params: loc=51.65798, scale=11.62282, shape=-0.02594891
# return_level([20, 100], ci="profile"):
#   estimate [84.883, 102.057]
#   lower    [77.811,  90.504]
#   upper    [97.962, 131.119]
# Return period of 105.4 mm: 138.3 years.
# tails.how_rare(depth, "2005-01-01", ci="profile", unit="mm", name="Québec City")
#   "A value of 105.4 mm in 2005 at Québec City is a 1-in-138-year event (95% CI: 30–1212 years)."

1-hour annual maximum 59.9 mm in 1979: single-duration GEV return period
129.1 years. 20- and 100-year 1-hour levels 39.67 and 56.75 mm (profile CIs
wide: 100-year 44.2–99.5 mm).

IDF on the same station, general scaling + Matérn Gaussian copula:
params (mu0, sigma0, xi, alpha, delta, nu, rho) ≈
(19.886, 5.706, -0.04467, 0.7143, 0.04461, 0.9168, 2.431)
100-year 1-hour intensity 43.61 mm/h, Wald 95% CI [39.46, 47.77].
scaling_test simple ≈ 0.00787 (reject); general ≈ 0.778 (compatible).

Batch: all 151 bundled stations, 24-hour maxima padded with NaN, all 151
GEV fits converged. Québec City's 100-year level in the batch equals the
single-station fit (102.0568 mm). Cap Tourmente 7041177 has nobs=11 and
ξ≈1.24; do not quote its 100-year level.

## Pitfalls

- scipy.stats.genextreme shape c equals minus tails/Coles ξ.
- First JAX call compiles (seconds); later calls are fast. Compiled kernels are cached on disk
  ($TAILS_CACHE/jax, default ~/.cache/tails/jax), so new sessions start warm. TAILS_JAX_CACHE=0 turns it off.
- Last axis is the record; preceding axes are the batch.
- Plot APIs: fit.plot_diagnostics() on GEVFit/GPDFit/POTFit; ReturnLevels.plot(); IDFFit.plot(). No GEVFit.plot().
- Do not put IDFCurves.jl author names in new public text; see NOTICE.
- Do not add a public planning document or a benchmark suite to this repository.
